contenido: Canon 1 Of the six holy and ecumenical synods that were gathered before us by the grace of God, and of their pious and divine definitions, and of their canons, which we have received as firm with the force of law, we also decree that they be firm, and as they constituted, so we also confess and preach.

The holy and great and ecumenical synod, gathered in Nicaea for the second time, by the grace of God and the pious decree of the Christ-loving emperors Constantine and Irene his mother: following the tradition of the Catholic Church, we define:

With all certainty and diligence we establish that, in a manner similar to the figure of the precious and life-giving cross, the venerable and holy images, both those of colors and tesserae and those of other convenient material, be proposed in the holy churches of God, and on the sacred vessels and vestments, and on the walls and boards, in the houses and on the roads: both, namely, the image of the Lord God and our Savior Jesus Christ, and of the untimely Lady our holy Mother of God, and of the honorable angels, and of all the saints together and of all men. The more frequently they are seen through imaginal formation, the more cunningly those who contemplate them rise to the memory and desire of their prototypes, and to pay them the kiss and the honorific adoration: not, however, to the true latria, which is according to faith and which only suits the divine nature; but according to what is offered to the figures of the precious and life-giving cross and to the holy Gospels and to the other sacred monuments, the offering of incense and lights in honor of these, as was also the custom of the ancient pious concession. Because the honor of the image passes to the prototype; and whoever adores the image, adores in it the subsistence of the person represented.

Thus, in effect, the doctrine of our holy Fathers is maintained, as a tradition of the Catholic Church, which receives the Gospel from one end of the earth to the other. Thus we follow Paul, who spoke in Christ, and the entire divine apostolic college and paternal holiness, retaining the traditions we received. Thus we prophetically sing the triumphal hymns of the Church: “Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion; announce, daughter of Jerusalem: rejoice and rejoice with all your heart. The Lord has removed from you the injustices of your adversaries; He has redeemed you from the hand of your enemies. The Lord is king in your midst: you will see no more evil, and peace will be upon you forever.

To those, then, who dare to feel or teach otherwise, or according to the criminal heretics to despise ecclesiastical traditions, and to invent any novelty, or to reject anything of what has been consecrated to the Church, be it the Gospel, or the figure of the cross, or imaginal painting, or the holy relics of the martyrs; or to perversely and cunningly invent something to subvert any of the legitimate traditions of the Catholic Church; and also to allocate sacred vessels or venerable monasteries to common use: if they are truly bishops or clerics, we order that they be deposed; and monks or lay people, who are segregated from communion.

Canon 6 Since there is a canon that says: "Twice a year in each province the canonical synod must be held by a meeting of the bishops," and because of the difficulty of the road and the lack of what is necessary for expenses, the holy Fathers of the sixth synod decreed that, removing all kinds of occasion and excuse, the synod be held once a year, and the wrong things be corrected: and we renew this. And if any prince forbids it, let him be excommunicated. And if any metropolitan neglects it, without necessity and violence and some reasonable cause, he will be subject to canonical penalties.

Canon 7 The divine Apostle Paul says: «The sins of some men are manifest, preceding judgment; and some also follow later. Preceding then the sins, other transgressions also follow. The impious heresy of the Christianomachs followed impiety, and other iniquity. Because just as they removed the aspect of the venerable images from the holy churches, so they also left some other customs, which should be renewed, and that they be done so according to the written and unwritten law. Therefore, any venerable temples that have been consecrated without the holy relics of the martyrs, we decree that the relics be replaced in them with the customary prayer. And if from now on any bishop consecrates a temple without the holy relics, let him be deposed, as one who has transgressed ecclesiastical traditions.

Canon 8 Since some of those who erred from Jewish superstition thought to mock Christ our God, falsely making themselves Christians, and denying him in secret and Sabbatizing and doing other Jewish things: we define that such should not be received either in communion, nor in prayer, nor in the church; but that they are manifestly Hebrews according to their religion; nor let their children be baptized, nor buy or own a servant. And if any of these are converted in sincere faith and confess from the heart, triumphing and reproving their customs and affairs, so that for this reason they may also argue and correct others: receive this one and baptize their children; and confirm them so that they stay away from Hebrew businesses. And if they are not like this, they will not be received in any way.

Canon 9 All the childish ludibrios and Bacchic delirium and the writings that have been composed against the venerable images must be delivered to the episcope of Constantinople, so that they may be replaced with the other heretical books. And if anyone is found hiding them, bishop or presbyter or deacon, let him be deposed; monk or layman, be anathematized.

Canon 10 Since some clerics, despising canonical ordination, distancing themselves from their parish, take refuge in another parish, and above all in this royal city preserved by God, and live alongside princes, celebrating the divine in their oratories: it is not lawful to receive them in any house or church without the will of the bishop himself and the bishop of Constantinople. And if anyone does this and perseveres in it, let him be deposed. And to those who dared to do this with the consent of those predicted, but not with canonical letters, and have distanced themselves from their church, we admonish them to return to their own. And if anyone does not do this, let him be excommunicated until he returns. And the same with the monks.

Canon 11 Everyone, both poor and rich, must have treasurers. And each bishop in his church elects the treasurer of his own clergy. And monks do the same in monasteries. And if someone does not do this, he is subject to the canonicals.

Canon 12 If any bishop or abbot gives any ecclesiastical possessions to the prince, or to another person, the gift is void. And if the bishop or the abbot does it, let him be deposed; the layman or monk be anathematized, until the things that were wrong are restored.

Canon 13 In the calamity that has been caused by our sins, many churches of holy men have been destroyed and secular habitations have been made. If, then, those who have them want to restore them as they were before, it is good and right; and if not, they be worthily corrected by canonical judgments. And if any bishop or abbot does this, let him be deposed; monk or layman be anathematized, as condemned by God, to whom "My house shall be called a house of prayer," and they made it a den of thieves.

Canon 14 That anointing in the order is not lawful for clerics without proof. And that it is not licit to ordain a clergyman in another's parish without letters from his bishop. That if anyone does this, both the one who ordered and the one ordered be deposed.

Canon 15 The cleric from now on is not ordained in two churches. Because it is a sign of negotiation and clumsy profit, and foreign to ecclesiastical custom. Because we have heard from the same voice of the Lord: «No one can serve two masters; for he will hate the one and love the other, or he will uphold the one and despise the other.” Let each one, therefore, according to the apostolic voice, remain in that which he has been called, and minister in one church. Because the things that are done in ecclesiastics for clumsy gain are alien to God. And for the correction of this, those that have hitherto been done of necessity, remain in the present; of the rest, however, do not do them. And if anyone after this definition tempts him, let him be deposed.

Canon 16 All luxury and ornamentation of the body is foreign to the priestly order and state. Those who, then, are bishops or clerics adorn themselves with resplendent and illustrious vestments, let them be corrected in this. And if they persevere in it, they will be subject to penalties. And the same goes for those who use ointments. For when the root of bitterness that springs upward, the heresy of the Christianomachs, became not only an abomination of the venerable painted images, but also contempt for all quietness and modesty and for what befits monks and clerics, "everything good" should be "restored to these things." If anyone, then, is found worthy of mocking laughter using ointments, let him be corrected. And if I persevere in it, I will be subject to the penalties.

Canon 17 Some monks, wanting to dominate and separate themselves from the yoke of the abbots, distancing themselves from their monasteries, try to build oratories, not having what is necessary to do so. If anyone, then, attempts to do this, let him be prohibited by the bishop of the place. And if he has what is necessary for the consummation, what he began may be brought to completion. And this is observed in everyone, both laymen and monks.

Canon 18 “It is not” “without crime” that “women” “cohabit” in episcopes or monasteries. If anyone, monk or clergyman, is caught admitting a woman to live in the monastery or episcope, let him be corrected; and if he does not cease, let him be deposed. And if something happens in the villas of the bishops or monasteries, and a woman wants to live there: let her not be prohibited by the monk or the clergy; if, however, she is without crime, and a servant of God.

Canon 19 The vituperable vice of covetousness has so prevailed among the rectors of the Church, that some of them, men and women, forgetting the precepts of the Lord: "Do not possess gold or silver or money in your areas," and "Freely you received, freely give," have become miserly. If any bishop or abbot or clergyman, then, for money lays on hands, or receives money for admission to the monastery: what has been done is void according to the great canon of Basil, and both he and the one who was promoted to the priesthood or monasticism by him are deposed, and in no way is he placed anywhere whose ordination or admission was done for money. Because “freely you received, freely give.” And the same of the treasurers and lawyers and paramonaries and of all those who are of the clergy, and of the monks: if they do something for clumsy gain, they should be deposed.

Canon 20 We define that double monasteries should not be made of the rest, because it causes scandal and offense to many. And if some with their relatives want to renounce and follow monasticism, the men enter the men's monastery, and the women enter the women's monastery. Because this pleases God and the holy Fathers. And those that exist until now, remain according to the rule of Saint Basil: monks and nuns do not live together in the same monastery. Because it is not fornication that is condemned, but rather the suspicion of fornication.
Canon 21 A monk or nun must not leave his or her monastery and go to another. And if he does this, it is advisable to host him; not, however, receive it without the consent of his abbot.

Canon 22 Offering all things to God and not being "servants of Mammon" is great. And if eating, monks or clerics observe not only the psalmody, but also silence: because "eating" and "drinking" they do so "for the glory of God." Do not "speak rude" or foolish things. And if anyone among monks or clerics does not observe this, let him be corrected.
